To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best segmentation algorithms are based on the Jensen–Shannon divergence and that the choice of a stopping criterion for the segmentation process has a strong impact on the performance of the segmentation algorithms.

(1) recursive segmentation algorithms based upon the Jensen-Shannon distance perform best, and (2) segmentation algorithms perform poorly in detecting short domains and domains with sharp transitions between neighboring domains.

(i) the recursive segmentation algorithm based on the Jensen Shannon divergence is a robust algorithm for segmenting genomic sequences, and that (ii) the performance of segmentation algorithms is sensitive to the choice of a segmentation stopping criterion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new benchmark and its use in the comparative testing of DNA segmentation methods.
a systematic and objective comparison of segmentation algorithms and with an assessment of their performances on simulated sequences.
the development of a reliable benchmark for testing segmentation algorithms and the evaluation of these algorithms on the benchmark.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
none of the existing algorithms are satisfactory, and that the problem of segmentation remains open.
no segmentation method is clearly superior to all other algorithms.
the performance of segmentation algorithms is still not satisfactory, and that more research is necessary to improve the accuracy and reliability of the results of segmentation algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of a segmentation algorithm is not as important as the choice of the segmentation stopping criterion.
the best segmentation algorithm is the algorithm with the best segmentation stopping criterion, which is not yet available.
the performance of segmentation algorithms is highly sensitive to the characteristics of the genomic sequence under consideration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the segmentation method should be guided by the specific application.
the performance of segmentation methods depends strongly on the characteristics of the sequences being analyzed.
the choice of segmentation algorithm is not as important as the choice of the segmentation-stopping criterion.
